text: {"memo": "Boeing’s most recently completed fiscal year, calendar 2024, showed a business still under pressure. Revenue was $91.57 billion, up about 7% from $83.62 billion in fiscal 2023, as defense offset weakness in commercial airplanes. GAAP net loss widened to $5.20 billion in 2024 from a $3.85 billion net loss in 2023. Adjusted operating margin stayed deeply negative, and free cash flow was negative in 2024 despite roughly $10.2 billion of operating cash flow. In fiscal 2023, revenue was $83.62 billion, net loss was $3.85 billion, and free cash flow was negative. In fiscal 2022, revenue was $79.08 billion and net loss was $4.62 billion. Boeing generated positive operating cash flow in both 2024 and 2023, but customer concentration, delivery charges, and inventory needs weighed on cash. The prior years showed similar margin pressure, with losses in 2020 and 2021 reflecting the pandemic and 737 MAX disruption. Over the last three fiscal years, revenue has risen from the low point yet profitability has not recovered. The stock should remain a high-risk turnaround name, though improving defense execution and potential commercial recovery are key catalysts."}
